_doc: HMTc Category 35 (Prepared and Packaged Meals) compiler config. Method v2.0, COMPOSITE form. Category 35 is composite: no credible government sets a contaminant maximum level for 'prepared meal' or 'vegetable stock', so each cell is a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS from the strictest applicable sovereign ML among the subcategory's PRINCIPAL COMPONENTS (component_read_across), a direct sovereign ML on the composite form (gov_ids -> regulatory-alignment; e.g. the canned-foods tin ML directly governs canned soup), a substantiated not-material determination, or a control. Component anchors are named register ids restricted to CREDIBLE regulators (EU, Codex, FDA, WHO/JECFA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK) and filtered for applicability: an adult prepared meal never reads across from an infant baby-food action level (infant/toddler mixed meals route to Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule). Basis: the composite is assessed as-consumed (ready-to-eat/ready-to-drink); wet-weight component MLs are comparable at face value and a dry-basis component ML applied at face value to a wet meal is conservative, so no basis conversion is performed. Numbers are NEVER occurrence-derived. Allowed provenance tags: regulatory-alignment, read-across, not-material, control, ratchet. See docs (CLAUDE.md Part 19) and the derivation report emitted alongside the compiled records. STAFF/HMTc content, not public wiki.
_doc_v1_1: v1.1 (2026-08-17) finished the two rows that v1.0 left incomplete (mixed-meals-prepared-foods, soups-broths-stocks). Hong Kong Cap. 132V was admitted to the credible-regulator set on 2026-08-17 (the bone-broth precedent), and its per-commodity Part 2 Schedule reaches components the EU, Codex and FSANZ leave unregulated. Net effect on those two rows: lead 100 -> 50 (Cap. 132V fruiting vegetables and preserved tomatoes), total arsenic 1000 -> 500 (Cap. 132V vegetables, cereals other than rice, meat, poultry), total mercury 500 -> 10 (Cap. 132V vegetables other than edible fungi), and total chromium off a factually false control onto a disclosed screen read-across at 500 (Cap. 132V vegetables other than pulses). CORRECTION OF THE v1.1 NOTE ITSELF: v1.1 claimed that the two Cap. 132V-falsified negative claims (no credible mercury ML for terrestrial meat, cereals or vegetables; no credible total-chromium ML for these components) were 'corrected rather than preserved'. That claim was true of the two composite rows only. Both falsehoods were PRESERVED on the bone-broth row, which v1.1 did not touch, and a third (no credible total-arsenic ML for meat) was preserved there as well. v1.2 corrects all three; see _doc_v1_2.

_category.name: Prepared and Packaged Meals
_category.basis_family: dietary as-consumed wet weight (the composite is assessed ready-to-eat or ready-to-serve; component maximum levels expressed as wet weight, as sold, as placed on the market, or as the portion ordinarily consumed are comparable at face value within this family)
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; COMPOSITE — disclosed read-across from strictest applicable principal-component sovereign ML; never occurrence-derived)
_category.method_note: COMPOSITE CONVENTION. No credible sovereign government sets a contaminant maximum level for a prepared meal, a soup, or a stock, so each numeric cell is the strictest applicable maximum level among the row's PRINCIPAL COMPONENTS, disclosed with the full candidate ladder and the binding component named. A component enters the candidate set when it is a principal (characterizing or major-mass) component of products within the row as scoped; an applicable but looser component value is disclosed and deliberately not adopted; and a stricter value scoped to a product form this category does not cover (infant and under-36-months foods, packaged drinking water, edible fats and oils, salt) is dispositioned in the cell's substantiation rather than silently adopted or silently ignored. Dry-basis and as-sold component values are applied at face value to the as-consumed composite, which is conservative, and no reconstitution conversion is invented (the 8:1 powder-to-liquid conversion is confined to infant formula).
_category.credible_note: Restated explicitly rather than widened: this set is identical to the compiler default. Hong Kong (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations, Cap. 132V) was admitted on 2026-08-17 on the bone-broth precedent, because its Part 2 Schedule is a comprehensive per-commodity metallic-contamination schedule that reaches commodities the EU, Codex and FSANZ leave unregulated: terrestrial-animal, vegetable and cereal mercury, vegetable and meat total arsenic, and total chromium in vegetables, pulses, cereals, meat and poultry. That admission is what finishes the two composite rows, because those Cap. 132V component values are stricter than the bindings v1.0 selected.

mixed-meals-prepared-foods.name: Mixed and prepared meals (frozen dinners, boxed meals, ready-to-eat)
mixed-meals-prepared-foods.basis_guard: wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|product as placed on market|food as listed in Cap 132V|as_sold
mixed-meals-prepared-foods.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a dietary food maximum level in a comparable as-consumed family (EU wet weight or product as placed on the market, FSANZ portion ordinarily consumed, Cap. 132V food as sold). The guard stops a drinking-water parametric value, an animal-feed maximum, a food-contact-material specific migration limit, or a toy migration limit from silently anchoring a composite food cell: those are different basis classes and are not comparable to a food-content ceiling. A cell whose named anchor falls outside the family fails the build instead of publishing a mixed-basis number. SCOPE OF WHAT THIS GUARD ACTUALLY DOES, corrected in v1.2: it refuses the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada drinking-water instruments, the EU 10/2011 specific migration limits, animal-feed maxima, and toy migration limits, because each carries a distinct basis string. It does NOT refuse the Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows, which share the single Cap. 132V basis string with that instrument's food rows and are therefore indistinguishable to a basis regex. Those rows are excluded by the stated ingredient-water determination and are named by id in each affected cell's companion set, not silently dropped.
mixed-meals-prepared-foods.scope_note: Adult and general-population frozen dinners, boxed meals, and ready-to-eat composite meals combining a starch/grain, a protein (meat, poultry, fish or other seafood, including aquatic invertebrates), vegetables, and often legumes/pulses and a dairy component. Infant and toddler mixed meals route to Category 1; a product that is primarily a single matrix (plain pasta, a single vegetable) routes to that matrix category. Bone broth is certified under Category 35 row bone-broth (mechanistically distinct hazard). Principal components for anchor selection are the starch or grain, the meat, poultry, fish or other seafood protein, the vegetables, the pulses or legumes, and the dairy fraction of cream-style and cheese-based variants. DAIRY IS A PRINCIPAL COMPONENT AND ITS CEILINGS ARE IMPORTED. v1.1 excluded dairy on the ground that it 'carries its own Category 24 milk ceilings at the ingredient stage'. That argument is not available, because this row applies the opposite rule to seafood: the seafood component is likewise governed at its own stage by the Category 6 seafood ceilings and its component maximum levels ARE imported into the ladder (fish lead 300, fish total mercury 500, seafood inorganic arsenic 100 and 50). No mass or characterizing test distinguishes the two. The composite convention admits a component when it is a principal (characterizing or major-mass) component of products within the row as scoped, and cream is a major-mass component of a bisque or chowder while cheese is the characterizing component of a macaroni-and-cheese or a cheese-sauced meal, exactly as the fish in a fish pie is. Dairy is therefore ADMITTED, and hk_cap132v_pb_milk_20 and hk_cap132v_pb_secondary-milk-products_20 (Cap. 132V Milk and Secondary milk products, 20 ug/kg lead each) enter the lead component set, which moves the published lead ceiling from 50 to 20 ug/kg. On total mercury the corresponding rows hk_cap132v_thg_milk_10 and hk_cap132v_thg_secondary-milk-products_10 are admitted at 10 ug/kg and tie with the binding vegetable value, so the published mercury ceiling is unchanged. On cadmium, total arsenic, nickel and total chromium no credible regulator publishes a dairy row at all, which is stated here rather than left as a silence. Cap. 132V Note 10 scopes Secondary milk products to products that are, or are reconstituted to be, ready to drink, so neither Cap. 132V row directly regulates cream or cheese; the milk value is the nearest applicable sovereign anchor for the dairy component and is adopted by disclosed read-across, which is what every other component on this row does and what Method v2.0 prescribes for an unregulated exact cell. The alternative considered and rejected was narrowing the row to exclude cream-style and cheese-based products; that would contradict this row's own product examples, would strand chowder, bisque and macaroni-and-cheese formats with no certifiable home, and is a Step 0 taxonomy decision rather than a limit-setting one.

component_read_across.label: the dairy component binds at 20 ug/kg (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, Milk and Secondary milk products), stricter than the fruiting-vegetable and preserved-tomato rows (50 each) that bound in v1.1 and stricter than the root/tuber vegetable (100), meat (100), cereal (200) and fish (300) components. Tightened from 100 to 50 in v1.1 on the Cap. 132V admission, and from 50 to 20 in v1.2 on the dairy ruling
component_read_across.substantiation: THE BINDING MOVED IN v1.2 BECAUSE THE DAIRY EXCLUSION DID NOT SURVIVE AUDIT. The ruling, the test that produced it, and the rejected alternatives are stated in full in this row's scope_note; in short, no mass or characterizing test distinguishes cream in a bisque or cheese in a macaroni-and-cheese from the seafood, meat and vegetable components already imported, so hk_cap132v_pb_milk_20 and hk_cap132v_pb_secondary-milk-products_20 are admitted and the ceiling is 20 ug/kg. CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY: a meal whose characterizing component is a cereal (Cap. 132V and FSANZ cereal lead 200) or a fish (EU 300) contains a component whose own sovereign ceiling is up to fifteen times this composite ceiling, so such a product may measure above it. That does not loosen the ceiling; the component is governed at its own stage by its own category, and a composite lot above 20 ug/kg lead is not certifiable on this row. The v1.1 ladder is retained and unchanged below the new binding: Cap. 132V sets lead at 50 ug/kg for fruiting vegetables (cucurbit and non-cucurbit alike) and for tomatoes preserved by heat treatment and hermetically sealed, which is the canned tomato base of most sauced prepared meals. Two stricter Cap. 132V lead rows remain deliberately NOT adopted and are now equal to rather than stricter than the binding: cereal-based food (20 ug/kg) and ready-to-eat complementary food other than cereal-based (20 ug/kg), both scoped to persons under the age of 36 months. This row certifies adult and general-population meals only; infant and toddler mixed meals route to HMTc Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule, so an under-36-months action level is not an applicable anchor here, and the Codex ready-to-eat meals for infants and young children ML (20 ug/kg) is dispositioned identically. Leafy-vegetable lead MLs (EU 2023/915 and Cap. 132V, 300 ug/kg each) and the fish ML (300) are applicable but looser and are disclosed rather than adopted. BEVERAGE-COMMODITY RULING, applied once and consistently across every analyte on this row. Fruit and vegetable juices, nectars, rice-based drinks, and bottled and packaged waters are separately regulated ready-to-drink beverage commodities, consumed as the whole product, and they are NOT principal components of a prepared meal, soup, broth or stock. Where a formulation contains juice or juice concentrate it enters as a minor flavour, sweetener or acidulant fraction of a few percent, exactly like the cooking fat and the salt this row already dispositions as ingredient specifications rather than composite ceilings, and the vegetable commodity that a vegetable juice is pressed from is already in the ladder at its own maximum level (Cap. 132V fruiting vegetables and preserved tomatoes), so adopting the juice row as well would import the same commodity twice in a form this row does not sell. The rows dispositioned by this ruling, named by id so the choice is auditable: eu2024_ni_juice_250 (nickel 250, fruit/vegetable juices and nectars) and eu2024_ni_juice_listed_1000 (nickel 1000); fda2023_ias_apple_juice_10 (inorganic arsenic 10, apple juice), eu2023_ias_fruit_juice_20 (inorganic arsenic 20) and eu2023_ias_rice_drinks_30 (inorganic arsenic 30, non-alcoholic rice-based drinks); eu2023_pb_fruit_juice_other_30, hk_cap132v_pb_fruit-juices-other-than-fruit-juices-exclusively-from-b_30 and hk_cap132v_pb_grape-juice_40 (lead 30 to 40); and the packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water parametric values dispositioned in the row scope note. THE RULING IS TESTED BY ITS CONSEQUENCE: if a juice were a principal component, the US apple-juice inorganic-arsenic action level of 10 ug/kg would become the ceiling for an entire prepared meal, which no sovereign anywhere has set and which would be an occurrence-free but nonsensical import. Adopting the nickel juice row at 250 while declining the inorganic-arsenic juice row at 10 is the asymmetry this remediation exists to remove, so both are declined under one stated rule. v1.2 REMOVES juice, nectar and drink from this row's audit_exclude_scope so these rows now surface in the compiler's stricter-unselected scan and in the publication gate's W1 warnings, where they are dispositioned by this paragraph rather than suppressed by a regex. Nothing else stricter is applicable: the by-hand scan of every credible live non-infant lead row below 20 ug/kg returns only drinking-water and bottled-water parametric values (5 to 10 ug/kg) and the EU 10/2011 plastics specific migration limit (10), both refused by this row's basis_guard as different basis families. INGREDIENT-WATER RULING, and a correction to what the basis_guard can actually do. The Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows sit in the SAME basis string as Cap. 132V's food rows ('food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule'), so this row's basis_guard does NOT filter them out even though it does filter the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada water instruments, whose basis strings are distinct. v1.2 corrects the earlier claim that the guard stops packaged-water values generally: the Cap. 132V water rows are excluded by DETERMINATION, not by the guard, and they are now named by id on every cell they could otherwise be read as binding. The determination: packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are a distinct beverage commodity, regulated as the sole daily hydration source and consumed by the litre, and formulation water is an INPUT SPECIFICATION rather than a principal component of the finished product. Certified lines are required to use potable water meeting the applicable national drinking-water standard, verified on the ingredient-water specification, rather than by re-deriving the composite ceiling from a water instrument. Applying a water parametric value as a food-content ceiling would hold a soup or a broth to a limit set for a product with a completely different daily intake, which no sovereign has done.

component_read_across.basis_label: read-across from strictest applicable principal-component total-arsenic ML (as consumed)
component_read_across.label: Cap. 132V sets a total-arsenic ML of 500 ug/kg for vegetables, for cereals other than rice, for meat of animal and for meat of poultry, which covers every principal component of a mixed meal and is stricter than the FSANZ cereal-grain ML (1000) that v1.0 selected. component_read_across.substantiation: TOTAL ARSENIC IS PUBLISHED HERE AS A PROTECTIVE SOVEREIGN MAXIMUM LEVEL, NOT AS A SCREEN. v1.1 opened this substantiation with 'Total arsenic is a non-toxicological screen' while the cell emitted an ordinary numeric read-across with no screen flag, so the prose and the provenance disagreed about whether the published number was protective and any renderer that distinguishes the two would have contradicted the cell's own text. The disagreement is resolved in favour of what the cell in fact publishes: Cap. 132V regulates total arsenic as a per-commodity protective ceiling, 500 ug/kg is the strictest applicable sovereign total-arsenic maximum level for the components of this row, and it is published as such. Total arsenic is one of the eight mandatory HMTc totals and is never satisfied by its species. The screen mechanism (`screen: true` with a screen_note) is used on this config only for total chromium, where the published value genuinely is not protective as a standalone total-element ceiling; it is not available on a component_read_across cell in this compiler in any case. The toxicologically dominant arsenic species, inorganic arsenic, is separately and far more strictly controlled on the iAs cell at 50 ug/kg (EU 2025/1891 cephalopods), and the species-below-total relation holds (iAs 50 <= tAs 500). v1.1 tightens the cell from 1000 to 500 ug/kg because the Cap. 132V per-commodity total-arsenic MLs reach the components for which the FSANZ cereal-grain ML was the only anchor, and the v1.0 claim that cereal grains carry the only credible total-arsenic component ML is withdrawn. Rice is deliberately absent from Cap. 132V's total-arsenic schedule because rice is regulated on inorganic arsenic instead; that is handled on the iAs cell and never by letting a species stand in for a total. The Cap. 132V edible-fats-and-oils total-arsenic ML (100 ug/kg) is stricter still and is NOT adopted: cooking fat is a minor formulation ingredient rather than a characterizing component of a meal, edible oils certify under HMTc Category 30 in their own basis, and holding a whole meal to an oil ceiling would import a limit from a material that is a few percent of the product. Food-grade salt (500) is dispositioned the same way, as an ingredient specification rather than a composite ceiling. control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury maximum level for this product form: authors2025-the-icp-ms-study-on-the-release-of and hwang2022-home-meal-replacement-heavy-metals measured methylmercury in this matrix, so the species is not absent and no not-material determination is supportable. component_read_across.substantiation: Nickel maximum levels are set by one credible instrument, Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 amending 2023/915 and applying from 2025-07-01. control.rationale: No credible regulator sets an aluminium maximum level for a prepared meal or for any principal component of one. mixed-meals-prepared-foods.material: Multi-component composite food. A starch or grain fraction (rice, pasta, noodle, potato, bread component), a protein fraction (meat, poultry, fish, or aquatic-invertebrate seafood), a vegetable fraction, frequently a pulse or legume fraction, a sauce or gravy fraction, and in cream-style and cheese-based variants a dairy fraction. Presented frozen, chilled, canned, retort-pouched or shelf-stable in a plastic or moulded-fibre tray, a retort pouch, a can, a board carton, or a film-sealed pack, and heated by the consumer in the pack.
mixed-meals-prepared-foods.components: COMPONENT-LEVEL SAMPLING PLAN. The certified unit is the production lot. (1) PRIMARY UNIT: the whole retail portion homogenised as consumed, after any consumer preparation step named on the pack, is the analytical unit for all eleven panel cells; a composite of not fewer than three retail units per lot, drawn across the lot's run. (2) SEPARATELY SAMPLED FRACTIONS, required whenever a panel result on the homogenate is materially above the line's established baseline for that formulation, so the source can be located rather than inferred: the starch or grain fraction, the protein fraction, the vegetable fraction, the pulse or legume fraction, the sauce or gravy fraction, and the dairy fraction. (3) SEAFOOD REFLEX: on any lot whose formulation contains fish or an aquatic invertebrate, the seafood fraction is retained for reflex methylmercury speciation (MeHg control cell) and reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation, and is analysed whenever total mercury or total arsenic on the homogenate approaches the published ceiling. (4) PACKAGING AND CONTACT SURFACES, which are the escalation targets for the aluminium and tin controls rather than routine analytical units: the tray or pouch and its lidding film or laminate, foil components, the can where the form is canned, and the aluminium cookware and contact surfaces of the production line. (5) INGREDIENT WATER, verified on specification against the applicable national drinking-water standard rather than by analysis of the composite.

not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury screen by closed-vessel acid digestion with ICP-MS or CV-AAS on the reconstituted as-served soup; reflex methylmercury speciation (species-specific isotope dilution GC-ICP-MS) only on a seafood-based soup whose total mercury approaches the total-mercury ceiling.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible regulator sets a methylmercury content limit for a composite soup, broth or stock; methylmercury MLs are scoped to individual fish species and to aquatic animals generally. MeHg is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), governed through the total-mercury cell at 10 ug/kg. EVIDENCE TEST, AND WHY THE TWO COMPOSITE ROWS OF THIS CATEGORY RESOLVE METHYLMERCURY DIFFERENTLY. hwang2022-home-meal-replacement-heavy-metals measured methylmercury directly in 480 Korean home-meal-replacement products and reported it BY MATRIX PHASE: detected in the non-fatty solid phase (mean 3.0, maximum 48.0 ug/kg) and the fatty solid phase, and NOT DETECTED in both the non-fatty liquid phase and the fatty liquid phase. A soup, broth or stock is the liquid phase, and a plated frozen dinner is the solid phase. That is why mixed-meals-prepared-foods holds methylmercury under mandatory analytical control (the species was measured in its matrix, so a not-material determination is not supportable there) while this row records a substantiated not-material determination with a reflex trigger. The asymmetry is evidence-driven and is recorded here rather than left to look like an inconsistency. Occurrence evidence is used only to test materiality, never to select a number (Method v2.0).

control.rationale: Inorganic tin is a tinplate migration pathway confined to the canned form, and three of the four forms this row certifies are not canned foods. The subcategory as scoped covers canned soups, dry soup mixes, bouillon cubes and powders, and ready-to-drink carton stocks and broths; the canned-foods tin maximum level reaches only the first. v1.1 published that ML as a row-wide firm ceiling of 250 mg/kg while its own label conceded that dry-mix, bouillon and carton-RTD forms have no tin migration pathway, so the compiled record asserted a 250 mg/kg tin ceiling for a carton broth that no instrument sets and the publication gate counted it as a firm protective limit. v1.2 converts the cell to the control + companion_ml pattern the other two rows of this category already use (mixed-meals-prepared-foods and bone-broth), so the canned form is verified against the ML while no ceiling is asserted for the forms the instrument does not reach. A form-split cell was considered and is not available in this compiler. A CANNED soup is verified against the canned-foods tin ML, on which three credible regulators converge at 250 mg/kg (250000 ug/kg): Codex CXS 193 (canned foods), FSANZ Schedule 19 (all canned foods) and HK Cap. 132V (canned food other than canned beverages), so the figure is not a single-jurisdiction artefact. The Cap. 132V canned-beverage row (150 mg/kg) is stricter but is not adopted: a ready-to-drink carton stock is not a canned beverage and has no tinplate contact, and a canned soup is a canned food under every one of these instruments. Instruments checked for the non-canned forms: EU 2023/915 (tin appears only as canned-food and canned-beverage MLs), Codex CXS 193, FSANZ Schedule 19, Cap. 132V, US FDA, Health Canada and UK dietary instruments; none sets a tin maximum level for a dry soup mix, a bouillon cube or a carton broth. THE STRICTEST APPLICABLE CANNED-FOOD TIN ML IS THE EU ROW AT 200 mg/kg, NOT THE 250 mg/kg FIGURE v1.1 NAMED. Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 sets tin at 200000 ug/kg (200 mg/kg) for canned foods other than canned beverages, except canned dried and canned powdered products (eu2023_sn_canned_foods_200000, basis product as placed on the market). It is stricter than the three rows v1.1 named as converging at 250 mg/kg (codex_cxs193_sn_canned_250000, aunz_sch19_sn_canned_250000, hk_cap132v_sn_canned-food-other-than-canned-beverages_250000), it is a credible-regulator maximum level in a basis this row accepts, and it was neither named nor dispositioned. This defect was found by hand during the v1.2 remediation and NOT by the compiler safety-net, because the soups row's audit_exclude_scope contained the term `beverage`, which matched the phrase 'canned beverages' inside the EU row's own scope string and suppressed it from every scan; the same class of regex self-defeat the v1.2 audit identified elsewhere. The term is removed. The canned form is verified against the EU value, and the EU instrument's own carve-out for canned dried and canned powdered products is independent confirmation that a tin maximum level does not reach a dry soup mix or a bouillon powder. Stricter still, and disclosed rather than adopted because they reach a different form: canned beverages at 100 mg/kg (eu2023_sn_canned_beverages_100000) and at 150 mg/kg (hk_cap132v_sn_canned-beverages_150000). Where a certified product is a canned drinkable broth presented as a beverage rather than a canned food, the canned-beverage value is the applicable one and the stricter of the two applicable rows governs; no single number is asserted across forms.
control.reference_method: Total tin by closed-vessel microwave acid digestion with ICP-MS, one determination per production lot, on the reconstituted as-served soup for dry-mix and bouillon forms and on the as-sold contents for canned and carton forms. A canned lot is verified against the canned-foods tin ML named in companion_ml. ESCALATION: any measurable tin on a dry-mix, bouillon or carton lot triggers packaging-source investigation (shared-line can or lid contact, tinned solder, foil or laminate liner, or a tin-bearing additive), with a confirmatory second lot before release.

control.rationale: No credible regulator sets an aluminium maximum level for a soup, stock or bouillon, or for any principal component of one. Instruments checked: EU 2023/915 and EU 2024/1987 (no aluminium entry), Codex CXS 193 (no aluminium entry), FSANZ Schedule 19 (aluminium appears only as infant-formula MLs of 500 and 1000 ug/kg, Category 1 scope), Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule (no aluminium entry), and US FDA, Health Canada and UK dietary instruments (no aluminium ML). Aluminium reaches the credible register only in basis families that cannot anchor a food-content cell: drinking-water parametric values (EU 2020/2184 and US 21 CFR 165.110 at 200 ug/L, Health Canada at 2900 ug/L), food-contact-material specific migration limits (EU 10/2011), and toy migration limits. Aluminium-containing additive maxima exist only in non-credible-tier instruments and are additive-use levels, not contaminant ceilings. Aluminium is therefore a mandatory reported cell with no invented ceiling.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by closed-vessel microwave acid digestion with ICP-MS on the reconstituted as-served soup, one determination per production lot, reported with no numeric pass/fail. Escalation: a result materially above the line's established baseline for that formulation triggers investigation of aluminium kettles, pans and contact surfaces, foil and laminate packaging including bouillon cube wrap, and any aluminium-containing additive, with a confirmatory second lot before release.

soups-broths-stocks.material: Multi-component composite food in four distinct physical forms that do not share a packaging pathway: canned soup in a tinplate or coated can; dry soup mix and bouillon cube or powder in a foil, laminate or paper wrap; and ready-to-drink stock or broth in an aseptic board carton, pouch or bottle. soups-broths-stocks.components: COMPONENT-LEVEL SAMPLING PLAN. The certified unit is the production lot, and the plan is form-dependent because this row's tin obligation is form-dependent. (1) PRIMARY UNIT: the product AS SERVED. A canned or carton lot is analysed as sold; a dry mix, bouillon cube or bouillon powder is reconstituted to the serving strength printed on the pack and analysed as the prepared broth, never as the concentrate, and the reconstitution ratio used is recorded on the certificate. (2) SEPARATELY SAMPLED FRACTIONS, required whenever a panel result on the as-served product is materially above the line's established baseline for that formulation: the vegetable fraction, the protein fraction, the cereal or noodle fraction, the pulse fraction, the dairy fraction, and the seasoning and salt fraction. (3) SEAFOOD REFLEX: on a bisque, chowder, fish stock or any seafood-containing formulation, the seafood fraction is retained for reflex methylmercury speciation and reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation, analysed whenever total mercury or total arsenic approaches the published ceiling. bone-broth.scope_note: Long-simmered stock made by extracting connective tissue and marrow from animal BONE (beef, chicken, pork). Mechanistically distinct from a vegetable or muscle-meat stock: bone is the body's principal lead reservoir, and lead partitions from bone into the broth during prolonged (often acidulated) simmering, so lead is the priority analyte and a generic stock limit understates the hazard. Certified as its own row, not the generic soups-broths-stocks row. Fish-bone broth (rare) inherits the Category 6 seafood ceilings for arsenic and mercury, which is why marine rows are excluded from this row's safety-net scan by determination rather than by accident. NO GOVERNMENT REGULATES THE EXACT CELL. No credible sovereign sets a contaminant maximum level for bone, bone extract, bone broth, gelatin or collagen: Hong Kong Cap. 132V Note 1 defines its animal commodities as the edible portion after removal of bones (if any) and fat from the meat, so Cap. 132V reaches the flesh and not the bone, and no EU, Codex, FSANZ, US, Canadian or UK instrument reaches bone either. Every numeric cell on this row is therefore a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS from the nearest applicable sovereign animal-tissue value, which is precisely what read-across is for, and the same ruling is applied to every cell of this row rather than cell by cell: the Cap. 132V animal rows anchor total arsenic, total mercury and total chromium, and the FSANZ and EU muscle-meat rows anchor lead and cadmium. A cell is a control here only where no credible regulator sets a value for ANY animal-derived component (nickel, aluminium), or where the pathway is a packaging one confined to a form the instrument does reach (tin).

Nothing stricter is applicable: the by-hand scan of every credible live non-infant total-mercury row below 50 ug/kg returns drinking-water, bottled-water and natural-mineral-water parametric values (1 to 2), the Cap. 132V Milk and Secondary milk products rows (10 each, not components of a bone broth), and the Cap. 132V vegetable and cereal rows (10 and 20, likewise not components of an animal-bone stock; they bind the two composite rows of this category instead). Methylmercury remains bounded by this total (MeHg <= tHg) and is reflex-speciated on an elevated total-mercury result. INGREDIENT-WATER RULING, and a correction to what the basis_guard can actually do. The Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows sit in the SAME basis string as Cap. 132V's food rows ('food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule'), so this row's basis_guard does NOT filter them out even though it does filter the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada water instruments, whose basis strings are distinct. v1.2 corrects the earlier claim that the guard stops packaged-water values generally: the Cap. 132V water rows are excluded by DETERMINATION, not by the guard, and they are now named by id on every cell they could otherwise be read as binding. The determination: packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are a distinct beverage commodity, regulated as the sole daily hydration source and consumed by the litre, and formulation water is an INPUT SPECIFICATION rather than a principal component of the finished product. Certified lines are required to use potable water meeting the applicable national drinking-water standard, verified on the ingredient-water specification, rather than by re-deriving the composite ceiling from a water instrument. Applying a water parametric value as a food-content ceiling would hold a soup or a broth to a limit set for a product with a completely different daily intake, which no sovereign has done. NON-COMPONENT DISPOSITION, run by hand across the whole register rather than through the row's scope regex, because a scope regex can only hide what it does not match. Every credible, live, non-infant, same-basis register row STRICTER than this cell's published value that is not an animal-tissue component is named in this cell's companion set and declined here, by class. (a) BEVERAGE COMMODITIES: the Cap. 132V and EU fruit-, grape- and berry-juice rows (30 to 50 ug/kg lead) and the packaged-water rows, none of which is an ingredient of a bone broth beyond the formulation water dealt with above. (b) PLANT COMMODITIES: the Cap. 132V fruiting-vegetable, preserved-tomato and canned-chestnut rows (50 each), the EU pulse row (cadmium 40) and the Cap. 132V cereal rows. Aromatic vegetables appear in some bone-broth formulations as a flavouring at a few percent and are strained out before packing, so they are a minor formulation ingredient rather than a principal (characterizing or major-mass) component; the product is bone, water and an acidulant, and a broth held to a fruiting-vegetable ceiling would take its limit from a material it does not substantially contain. A bone broth whose formulation is genuinely vegetable-characterized is not this row's product and certifies as a soup or stock under row soups-broths-stocks, where those vegetable values do bind. (c) DAIRY: the Cap. 132V Milk and Secondary milk products rows (lead 20, total mercury 10). Dairy IS admitted as a principal component on the two composite rows of this category, on the mass and characterizing test stated in their scope notes, and it is declined here for the opposite reason under the same test: a bone broth contains no dairy fraction at all. (d) RENDERED FATS: the Cap. 132V edible-fats-and-oils and fat-spread rows (lead 80, total arsenic 100). Adhering and rendered fat is skimmed rather than sold, and edible fats and oils certify under HMTc Category 30 in their own basis. (e) UNDER-36-MONTHS ROWS: the Cap. 132V cereal-based-food and ready-to-eat complementary-food rows (20 each), which route to HMTc Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule and are not applicable anchors for a general-population product.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in a terrestrial-animal bone broth and is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg). It is bounded by the total-mercury cell. Only a seafood-derived bone broth carries a methylmercury pathway, and that inherits the Category 6 seafood ceiling.
not_material.reference_method: Bounded by the published total-mercury ceiling of 50 ug/kg (tHg cell). REFLEX TRIGGER: methylmercury speciation by species-specific isotope dilution GC-ICP-MS on any lot whose total mercury approaches the published total-mercury ceiling, and on any fish-bone broth regardless of total mercury.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible regulator sets a methylmercury content limit for meat, bone or terrestrial animal-derived stock; the credible methylmercury limits are the US FDA CPG 540.600 action level for fish, shellfish, crustaceans and other aquatic animals (1000 ug/kg) and the Cap. 132V fish-species rows (fish, fish balls and fish cakes 500; orange roughy 800; pink cusk-eel 1000; tuna 1200; alfonsino 1500; shark 1600; marlin 1700 ug/kg), every one of which is an aquatic-animal instrument and every one of which is looser than this row's published total-mercury read-across of 50 ug/kg, so none can bind. MeHg is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), now a disclosed read-across of 50 ug/kg (HK Cap 132V meat of animal).
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; Codex CXS 193; US FDA CPG 540.600 (methylmercury action level for fish, shellfish, crustaceans and other aquatic animals, 1000 ug/kg); FSANZ Schedule 19; Health Canada; UK; HK Cap 132V fish-species methylmercury rows. None sets a methylmercury limit for a terrestrial-animal bone broth, and every one that exists is scoped to aquatic animals and is looser than the 50 ug/kg total-mercury ceiling published here.

control.reference_method: Total nickel by closed-vessel microwave acid digestion with ICP-MS on the homogenised as-consumed broth, one determination per production lot, reported on the certificate with no numeric pass/fail. ESCALATION: a result materially above the line's established baseline for that formulation triggers investigation of nickel-bearing stainless-steel kettles, valves and transfer lines (long hot extraction times are the plausible pathway in a simmered stock), of the ingredient water, and of any plant-matrix additions to the formulation, with a confirmatory second lot before release.

control.rationale: Inorganic tin is a tinplate migration pathway confined to the canned form; carton (RTD), frozen and refrigerated bone broth have no tin source, so no ceiling is asserted for them. A CANNED bone broth is verified against the canned-foods tin ML, on which three credible regulators converge at 250 mg/kg (250000 ug/kg): Codex CXS 193 (canned foods), FSANZ Schedule 19 (all canned foods) and HK Cap. 132V (canned food other than canned beverages). Instruments checked for a non-canned form: EU 2023/915 (tin appears only as canned-food and canned-beverage MLs), Codex CXS 193, FSANZ Schedule 19, Cap. 132V, US FDA, Health Canada and UK dietary instruments; none sets a tin maximum level for a broth outside a can. The Cap. 132V canned-beverage row (150 mg/kg) is stricter but is not adopted: a ready-to-drink carton broth is not a canned beverage and has no tinplate contact. THE STRICTEST APPLICABLE CANNED-FOOD TIN ML IS THE EU ROW AT 200 mg/kg, NOT THE 250 mg/kg FIGURE v1.1 NAMED. Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 sets tin at 200000 ug/kg (200 mg/kg) for canned foods other than canned beverages, except canned dried and canned powdered products (eu2023_sn_canned_foods_200000, basis product as placed on the market). It is stricter than the three rows v1.1 named as converging at 250 mg/kg (codex_cxs193_sn_canned_250000, aunz_sch19_sn_canned_250000, hk_cap132v_sn_canned-food-other-than-canned-beverages_250000), it is a credible-regulator maximum level in a basis this row accepts, and it was neither named nor dispositioned. This defect was found by hand during the v1.2 remediation and NOT by the compiler safety-net, because the soups row's audit_exclude_scope contained the term `beverage`, which matched the phrase 'canned beverages' inside the EU row's own scope string and suppressed it from every scan; the same class of regex self-defeat the v1.2 audit identified elsewhere. The term is removed. The canned form is verified against the EU value, and the EU instrument's own carve-out for canned dried and canned powdered products is independent confirmation that a tin maximum level does not reach a dry soup mix or a bouillon powder. Stricter still, and disclosed rather than adopted because they reach a different form: canned beverages at 100 mg/kg (eu2023_sn_canned_beverages_100000) and at 150 mg/kg (hk_cap132v_sn_canned-beverages_150000). Where a certified product is a canned drinkable broth presented as a beverage rather than a canned food, the canned-beverage value is the applicable one and the stricter of the two applicable rows governs; no single number is asserted across forms.
control.reference_method: Total tin by closed-vessel microwave acid digestion with ICP-MS on the homogenised as-consumed broth, one determination per production lot. A canned lot is verified against the canned-foods tin ML named in companion_ml. ESCALATION: any measurable tin on a non-canned form triggers packaging-source investigation (can or lid substitution on a shared line, tinned-solder contact, or a tin-bearing additive), with a confirmatory second lot before release.

control.rationale: No credible regulator sets an aluminium maximum level for bone broth, for any animal-derived stock, or for any animal-tissue component of one. Instruments checked: EU 2023/915 and EU 2024/1987 (no aluminium entry), Codex CXS 193 (no aluminium entry), FSANZ Schedule 19 (aluminium appears only as infant-formula MLs of 500 and 1000 ug/kg, which are Category 1 scope), Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule (no aluminium entry), and US FDA, Health Canada and UK dietary instruments (no aluminium ML). Aluminium reaches the credible register only in basis families that cannot anchor a food-content cell: drinking-water parametric values (EU 2020/2184 and US 21 CFR 165.110 at 200 ug/L, Health Canada at 2900 ug/L), food-contact-material specific migration limits (EU 10/2011, a migration figure into a simulant), and toy migration limits. Permitted-additive maxima for aluminium-containing additives exist only in non-credible-tier instruments and are additive-use levels rather than contaminant ceilings. Aluminium is therefore a mandatory reported cell with no invented ceiling; Tier-2 analyte.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by closed-vessel microwave acid digestion with ICP-MS on the homogenised as-consumed broth, one determination per production lot, reported on the certificate with no numeric pass/fail. ESCALATION: a result materially above the line's established baseline for that formulation triggers investigation of aluminium stockpots, kettles and contact surfaces, of foil and laminate packaging including pouch and carton liners, and of any aluminium-containing additive, with a confirmatory second lot before release.

read_across.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets total chromium at 1000 ug/kg for meat of animal and for meat of poultry, the nearest applicable sovereign animal-tissue value for a bone-derived stock; the cell publishes it as a SCREEN. v1.2 replaces a control whose stated reason was false
read_across.substantiation: v1.1 recorded this cell as a bare control on the statement that no credible regulator sets a total-chromium maximum level for bone broth. THAT STATEMENT IS FALSE, and it is the same statement that v1.1 itself identified as false and corrected on the other two rows of this category: both composite rows carry the sentence 'v1.0 recorded this cell as a bare control on the statement that no credible regulator sets a total-chromium maximum level ... That statement is false following Hong Kong's admission to the credible-regulator set on 2026-08-17.' Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule item 7 sets total chromium at 1.0 mg/kg (1000 ug/kg) for Meat of animal and for Meat of poultry. A published standard that retains, on a live row, a factual claim it documents as false elsewhere in the same compiled directory is the single easiest thing for opposing counsel to put in front of a jury, so the falsehood is corrected rather than preserved and the v1.1 note that overclaimed the correction is itself corrected (see _doc_v1_1 and _doc_v1_2). Cap. 132V Note 1 excludes bone from these commodities, so this is a disclosed READ-ACROSS from the nearest applicable sovereign animal-tissue value, ruled once for this row and applied identically to total arsenic and total mercury. The looser and stricter Cap. 132V total-chromium rows are disclosed and not adopted for opposite reasons: meat of poultry at 1000 is equal, and vegetables other than pulses at 500 and pulses, cereals and fish at 1000 are not components of an animal-bone stock (they bind the two composite rows instead). Nothing stricter is applicable: the by-hand scan of every credible live non-infant total-chromium row below 1000 ug/kg returns the EU 10/2011 plastics specific migration limit (10), drinking-water, bottled-water and natural-mineral-water parametric values (25 to 100), and the Cap. 132V vegetable row (500), none of which is an animal-tissue component and all of which the basis_guard would refuse. IT PUBLISHES AS A SCREEN: dietary chromium is overwhelmingly trivalent (an essential nutrient) and the health-relevant hexavalent species is separately determined not material in a cooked, wet, protein-rich broth (Cr-VI cell, speciation-bounded), so the value is not protective as a standalone total-element ceiling. Total chromium remains mandatory on every lot. ESCALATION: a result approaching the screen value is treated as a stainless-steel equipment-leaching signal, investigated against kettle and transfer-line contact time and temperature (a bone broth simmers for many hours, which is the longest hot-metal contact of any row in this category), with a confirmatory second lot before release, and not as a toxicological finding. The Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows sit in the SAME basis string as Cap. 132V's food rows ('food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule'), so this row's basis_guard does NOT filter them out even though it does filter the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada water instruments, whose basis strings are distinct. v1.2 corrects the earlier claim that the guard stops packaged-water values generally: the Cap. 132V water rows are excluded by DETERMINATION, not by the guard, and they are now named by id on every cell they could otherwise be read as binding. The determination: packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are a distinct beverage commodity, regulated as the sole daily hydration source and consumed by the litre, and formulation water is an INPUT SPECIFICATION rather than a principal component of the finished product. Certified lines are required to use potable water meeting the applicable national drinking-water standard, verified on the ingredient-water specification, rather than by re-deriving the composite ceiling from a water instrument. Applying a water parametric value as a food-content ceiling would hold a soup or a broth to a limit set for a product with a completely different daily intake, which no sovereign has done.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is a screen, not a protective ceiling: the value records the sovereign total-chromium ML (Cap. 132V meat of animal, 1000 ug/kg) while the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which is not stable in this matrix. The cert standards renderer is the consumer that excludes a screen cell from the firm-limit count it displays; the deterministic publication gate in this repo (tools/standards/audit-compiled-standards.mjs) counts screen cells toward its own firm total, so the two counts differ by design and neither is wrong. The escalation rule is equipment-leaching investigation, not a toxicological exceedance.
Cr.basis_label: read-across from the sovereign total-chromium animal-meat ML (Cap. 132V, food as sold, applied at face value to the as-consumed broth)

not_material.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is reduced to Cr-III in a cooked, wet, protein-rich broth; a Cr-VI result is an artifact of the total-chromium screen. No credible regulator sets a Cr-VI food ML.
not_material.reference_method: Cr-VI is not measured routinely; total chromium (Cr cell) is the reported screen at 1000 ug/kg and bounds any hexavalent fraction. REFLEX TRIGGER: Cr-VI speciation by ion-chromatography ICP-MS only where a total-chromium result approaches the screen value AND the equipment-leaching investigation does not account for it.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible regulator sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food; Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in a cooked, wet, protein-rich broth and any Cr(VI) signal is an artifact of the total-chromium screen. Cr(VI) is a species of and bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr), now a published screen read-across of 1000 ug/kg (HK Cap 132V meat of animal), so the bound is numeric rather than open.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; Codex CXS 193; US FDA; FSANZ; Health Canada; UK; HK Cap 132V — none set a hexavalent-chromium content limit for food.

bone-broth.basis_guard: wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|product as placed on market|food as listed in Cap 132V|as_sold
bone-broth.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a dietary food maximum level in a comparable as-consumed family (EU wet weight or product as placed on the market, FSANZ portion ordinarily consumed, Cap. 132V food as sold). v1.2 adds the guard this row previously left null. It matters here for the same reason it matters on the soup row: a bone broth is mostly water, so a packaged-drinking-water parametric value would look superficially comparable and is not. The drinking-water and bottled-water rows that sit below several of this row's bindings (lead 5 to 10, cadmium 3 to 7, total arsenic 10, total mercury 1 to 2, total chromium 25 to 100 ug/kg) govern water sold as the sole daily hydration source, and the EU 10/2011 rows below them are specific migration limits into a food simulant. Neither is a food-content ceiling. A cell whose named anchor falls outside the family fails the build instead of publishing a mixed-basis number. SCOPE OF WHAT THIS GUARD ACTUALLY DOES, corrected in v1.2: it refuses the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada drinking-water instruments, the EU 10/2011 specific migration limits, animal-feed maxima, and toy migration limits, because each carries a distinct basis string. It does NOT refuse the Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows, which share the single Cap. 132V basis string with that instrument's food rows and are therefore indistinguishable to a basis regex. Those rows are excluded by the stated ingredient-water determination and are named by id in each affected cell's companion set, not silently dropped.
bone-broth.material: Single-component animal extract. Long-simmered stock made by extracting connective tissue, collagen and marrow from animal BONE (beef, chicken, pork), with adhering meat and fat, water, an acidulant such as vinegar in most formulations, and aromatic vegetables and salt in some. Presented as a refrigerated or frozen liquid, a shelf-stable carton, pouch or can, or a dried powder or concentrate.
bone-broth.components: COMPONENT-LEVEL SAMPLING PLAN. The certified unit is the production lot, and lead is the priority analyte because bone is the animal's principal lead reservoir and the extraction step is the hazard. (1) PRIMARY UNIT: the broth as consumed. A liquid lot is analysed as sold; a dried or concentrated lot is reconstituted to the serving strength printed on the pack and analysed as the prepared broth, with the ratio recorded on the certificate. A composite of not fewer than three retail units per lot, drawn across the run, for all eleven panel cells, with MANDATORY per-lot lead testing rather than skip-lot. (2) SEPARATELY SAMPLED INPUTS, required on any lot whose lead is materially above the line's established baseline and on every new bone supplier before first certification: the incoming bone by species and skeletal site, the adhering meat and fat, the acidulant, the aromatic vegetable fraction where present, and the extraction water. Bone lead varies by animal age and husbandry, so the bone input is the first escalation target and a supplier change is a re-qualification event. (3) EXTRACTION-PARAMETER RECORD, retained with the lot because it drives partition rather than being an analyte: simmer time, temperature and the acidulant concentration and pH. (4) EQUIPMENT AND PACKAGING, the escalation targets for the chromium screen and the nickel, aluminium and tin controls: the stainless-steel kettle, valves and transfer lines with their hot-contact time (the longest of any row in this category), aluminium stockpots and contact surfaces, foil and laminate packaging, and the can where the form is canned. (5) FISH-BONE BROTH, if produced on the line, is out of this row's scope for arsenic and mercury and inherits the Category 6 seafood ceilings; it is sampled separately and never composited with a terrestrial-bone lot.

_doc_v1_2: v1.2 (2026-08-17) is an adversarial-audit remediation covering all three rows, including bone-broth. BLOCKERS FIXED. (1) bone-broth total arsenic was a control asserting that no credible regulator sets a total-arsenic ML for meat, bone or animal-derived stock; Cap. 132V sets 500 ug/kg for meat of animal, meat of poultry, edible offal of animal and edible offal of poultry, and the same row already reads across from the same Cap. 132V meat-of-animal family on its mercury cell, so the cell is now a disclosed component read-across publishing 500. (2) bone-broth total chromium was a control asserting that no credible regulator sets a total-chromium ML for bone broth; Cap. 132V sets 1000 ug/kg for meat of animal and meat of poultry, so the cell is now a disclosed screen read-across publishing 1000. (3) the composite rows' inorganic-arsenic cells bound at 100 from the EU fish-other row while EU 2025/1891 sets 50 for cephalopods, an aquatic-invertebrate component the rows' own mercury substantiations name (prawn stir-fry, clam chowder, lobster bisque); cephalopods are adopted and both rows now publish inorganic arsenic at 50, with the full EU 2025/1891 seafood ladder disclosed. MAJORS FIXED. bone-broth's nickel control cited EU 2024/1252 for maximum levels that are Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987, and its tAs/Ni/Al/Cr controls carried no instruments-checked enumeration and no escalation rule; the mercury-speciation completeness claim on soups-broths-stocks omitted the US FDA CPG 540.600 aquatic-animal action level while its own jurisdictions-checked string named that instrument; the nickel substantiations presented a closed enumeration of EU 2024/1987 that omitted the juice/nectar and pulse rows; soups-broths-stocks published the canned-foods tin ML as a row-wide firm ceiling on a row whose scope covers dry mix, bouillon and carton RTD, three forms no cited instrument reaches, and is now the control + companion_ml pattern the other two rows already use; and the dairy exclusion in both composite scope notes rested on an argument ('governed at its own stage in its own category') that the same rows do not apply to seafood. THE DAIRY RULING IS THE ONE THAT MOVES A NUMBER: no mass or characterizing test distinguishes cream in a chowder or cheese in a macaroni-and-cheese from the components already admitted, so dairy is ADMITTED rather than excluded and lead moves from 50 to 20 ug/kg on both composite rows (Cap. 132V Milk and Secondary milk products, 20 each). MINORS FIXED. The bone-broth lead substantiation stated the accumulating-tissue analog as a single FSANZ figure of 500 when the cross-jurisdiction ladder is 100 to 500 (Cap. 132V offal of poultry 100, pig 150, cattle 200). The composite total-arsenic cells described their own published number as a non-toxicological screen while emitting it as an ordinary protective limit; the prose is corrected to what the cell in fact publishes, the strictest applicable sovereign total-arsenic maximum level, because this compiler supports `screen` only on gov_ids and read_across cells and not on component_read_across. The total-chromium screen_note no longer asserts an unqualified exclusion from the firm-limit count; it names the consumer that performs the exclusion. SAFETY-NET REGEXES WIDENED so the compiler scan can see the rows this audit found by hand: bone-broth gains Cap. 132V commodity phrasings (meat of animal, meat of poultry, edible offal of animal, edible offal of poultry) plus gelatin, collagen and bone, and the basis_guard the composite rows already carried; both composite rows gain aquatic-invertebrate, dairy and juice/nectar terms, and juice, nectar and drink are REMOVED from audit_exclude_scope so a beverage-commodity row is dispositioned in prose by id rather than suppressed by a regex. NOT DONE, AND DELIBERATELY: the audit's request to make audit-compiled-standards.mjs W1 recompute the stricter-row scan independently of the compiled record is a change to a shared publication gate used by every category in this batch and is out of scope for a single-category remediation; until it lands, a 0-FAIL gate run on this directory is NOT evidence that no stricter applicable sovereign row exists, and the independent by-hand scan recorded in each cell's substantiation is what carries that claim. ONE DEFECT THE ADVERSARIAL AUDIT DID NOT FIND, DISCOVERED DURING THE REMEDIATION AND FIXED HERE: the tin cell on soups-broths-stocks published 250 mg/kg as its firm ceiling from Codex, FSANZ and Cap. 132V while Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 sets 200 mg/kg for canned foods other than canned beverages (eu2023_sn_canned_foods_200000), a stricter credible-regulator maximum level in an accepted basis that was neither named nor dispositioned. It was invisible to the compiler scan because the row's audit_exclude_scope contained `beverage`, which matched the phrase 'canned beverages' inside the EU row's own scope string. So the published number was BOTH too loose for the canned form and asserted over three forms no instrument reaches. All three rows of this category now name the EU 200 mg/kg row as the canned-form companion, with the 250 mg/kg rows and the stricter canned-beverage rows (EU 100, Cap. 132V 150) disclosed alongside. This is the concrete evidence for the caveat above: a green compiler run and a 0-FAIL gate run are not evidence that no stricter applicable sovereign row exists, because both inherit the config's regexes.
